# Dataset Report — Nexar Dashcam Collision Prediction
<!-- generated by scripts/prepare_dataset.py -->

## Source, access, licence
- Hugging Face `nexar-ai/nexar_collision_prediction` (gated; access granted to the user's account), from the Nexar challenge (Moura, Zhu, Zvitia, CVPR-W 2025, arXiv 2503.03848).
- Licence: **Nexar Open Data License**. Free use with attribution; no resale, no re-identification of people or vehicles, no use in harmful systems. Videos are not redistributed with this project.

## Structure (verified)
- `train/positive/*.mp4` + `train/positive/metadata.csv`; `train/negative/*.mp4` + `train/negative/metadata.csv`.
- Raw metadata columns: file_name, time_of_event, time_of_alert, light_conditions, weather, scene, time_to_accident (canonicalised to: video_id, label, time_of_event, time_of_alert, light_conditions, weather, scene). There is **no label column**: the class is defined by the folder (positive = collision or near-collision, negative = normal driving). `time_to_accident` is empty in train.
- Full train annotation: 1500 rows (750 positive / 750 negative). Every positive has time_of_event: True; time_of_alert ≤ time_of_event everywhere: True.
- Collision and near-collision are **not** distinguished by separate labels, so the task is binary.

## Split (video-level, stratified, no leakage)
| split | videos | positive | negative |
|---|---|---|---|
| train | 280 | 140 | 140 |
| val | 60 | 30 | 30 |
| test | 60 | 30 | 30 |

Windows are cut only inside each split's own videos (see EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.md), and positive windows always end before time_of_event.

## Full dataset (v3, 2026-11-19)
- All **1,500** Nexar training videos were downloaded (24 GB), under the same Nexar Open Data License as above: attribution, no resale,
  no re-identification. The videos are not redistributed with this project.
- Quality check (`scripts/prepare_full_split.py` → `data/processed/validation_full.json`): all 1,100 new videos are readable, and none
  has an annotation inconsistency (event beyond duration, or alert after event).
- Labels are unchanged: the class comes from the positive/negative folder, with `time_of_event` / `time_of_alert` from `metadata.csv`
  (750 positives / 750 negatives).
- Statistics (`data/processed/dataset_stats_full.json`):

  | Statistic | Value |
  |---|---|
  | Duration | mean 37.7 s (14–60 s) |
  | Resolution | 1280×720 for all videos |
  | Alert lead (event − alert) | median 1.43 s (0.03–4.47 s) |
  | Light | Normal 1,355 / Twilight 88 / Dark 47 / Bright 10 |
  | Weather | Clear 919 / Cloudy 495 / Rain 83 / Snow 1 / missing 2 |
- **Split** (pre-declared, `data/processed/splits_full.json`):
  - the original 400-video split is unchanged;
  - the 1,100 new videos were divided label-stratified (seed 2026) into **dev_new 936** and **test_ext 164**.
  - Development = train + val + dev_new = **1,276 videos**.
  - Held-out = original test (60) + test_ext (164) = **224 videos**, never used for any choice.
  - Splits are by video, with no overlap (asserted).
